notes: Criminal appeal over theft-from-a-house punishment; court quotes dictionary definitions of 'inhabitant,' 'lodger,' and 'boarder' only to decide whether a boarder qualifies as a 'domestic servant or other inhabitant' under the burglary/theft statute (favoring lighter punishment). Does not address the lawfulness, character, or regulation of letting rooms/dwellings for pay.
Concerns whether a canvas tent qualifies as a 'house' under the disorderly-house (prostitution) statute; not a boarding/lodging house case and does not bear on compensated occupancy of a dwelling.

Weapons-carrying prosecution turning on whether defendant could claim the 'own premises' exception while land was under an agricultural lease to a tenant; general landlord-tenant possession doctrine, not about lodging/boarding letting.
Indictment-sufficiency ruling on the disorderly-house (prostitution) statute's 'owner, lessee, or tenant' element; concerns houses of prostitution, not lodging/boarding houses.
Rents-for-enclosed-pastureland dispute between cattle companies; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding issue.
Grazing-land lease holdover-tenant rent dispute; not a dwelling/lodging letting case.
Adverse-possession/limitation-title dispute over public domain land; no lodging or letting issue.

Fire-insurance dispute over whether a commercial storehouse (saddlery/printing office, later furniture store/restaurant) was 'vacant' during a change of commercial tenants; concerns insurance-policy construction of vacancy, not residential lodging/boarding letting.

Property-tax exemption dispute over a residence used partly as a girls' day/boarding school run by owner's wife; a boarding *school*, not compensated lodging/boarding of paying occupants, and turns on tax-exemption construction.
Trespass-to-try-title dispute over removal of a fixture (shoemaker's shop) erected by a sub-tenant during pending litigation; no lodging/boarding issue.
Forcible entry and detainer procedural standing dispute (who may sue when a tenant's possession is invaded); not about lodging/boarding letting.
Habeas corpus case on a foreign national's domicile for Confederate conscription purposes; unrelated to letting of dwellings/rooms.
Complex will-construction, forced-heirship, and limitations dispute over urban lots; no lodging/boarding letting issue.

holding_summary: A landlord's agent notified a holdover tenant, who leased the house to run a boarding-house business, before the lease term ended that any continued occupancy would be month-to-month only. The court held that this notice defeated any implied one-year renewal despite the tenant's continued rent payments, so the landlord could recover possession without further notice.

quotes.text: Shipman’s damages were predicated upon the loss-and inconvenience occasioned him by the interference with his business as a boarding-house keeper carried on by him on the premises, having, as he charged, with Mrs. Mitchell’s knowledge obtained and acquired Mrs. Williams’ lease for the purpose of carrying on the boardinghouse business.

If, however, at or before the expiration of the former lease, the tenant was informed that he would not be permitted, after the expiration of that lease, to occupy the rented premises otherwise than as a tenant from month to month, and not for a year, then no contract that he should occupy the property for a year could be implied
Shipman sued Mitchell for damages on breach of an implied contract.

notes: Tenant acquired the landlord's leasehold specifically to run a boarding house, with landlord's knowledge/consent; court applies ordinary landlord-tenant doctrine to the arrangement without any suggestion the boardinghouse use was improper or requiring special license -- background support for letting as an ordinary commercial use, though the holding itself turns on notice/implied-renewal, not on the boardinghouse's legality.
Homestead-abandonment/partition dispute among decedent's heirs; land was rented to tenants, but the case is about homestead-use continuity, not lodging/boarding.

Nuisance suit against a landlord for knowingly renting houses to prostitutes for use as places of prostitution; concerns liability for renting property to be used for an illegal vice trade, not the lawfulness or regulation of lodging/boarding-house letting.

Premises-liability suit over an injury from a defective passageway between rented second-story rooms (bed rooms/offices); rented rooms are background facts in a landlord-vs-tenant tort-duty ruling, not an adjudication of the lodging arrangement's legal character.
Public-land pre-emption/estoppel dispute; a witness had briefly held land as a tenant, but the case does not concern lodging or boarding letting.
